summary: mutex-forge ships a hidden Slack/Ethereum-driven RCE backdoor with host exfil
details: The package presents itself as a mutex/semaphore utility but contains a hidden staging chain. lib/Mutex.js has a covert branch in runExclusive: when the caller's callback carries meta.jobId === 'cross-chain-transfer', it detaches `node lib/withLoad.min.js cross-chain-transfer`. lib/withLoad.min.js is an obfuscator.io-style string-array bundle that long-polls Slack conversations.history and reads an Ethereum Sepolia contract (0xE390863Dac96a7118C71227C2b099B50cF602D31) via Alchemy/Infura, reassembles chunked ciphertext, PBKDF2-derives a key, AES-GCM decrypts to JavaScript, writes it to lib/Mutex.js, chmods 755, and spawns it with process.execPath — a persistent remote-code delivery channel controlled by whoever posts to the attacker's Slack channel. The same loader collects host reconnaissance (os.platform/release/arch/hostname/cpus/totalmem/freemem/uptime) and POSTs it to slack.com /api/chat.postMessage and api.telegram.org /bot<token>/sendMessage, authenticating with hardcoded base64-encoded Slack xoxb bot tokens and a Telegram bot token embedded in the bundle. Anti-forensics is built in: the loader unlinks itself and its sibling droppers (withLoad.min.d.js, tryLoad.min.d.js), edits lines out of Mutex.js, and strips a marker line from../LICENSE to hide the trojanized state.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
